sections.h2: How big is Aurora, and which counties does it cover?
sections.html:
Aurora sits on the Fox River in northeastern Illinois and is the second most populous city in the state after Chicago. The 2020 census counted 180,542 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 181,505. It is also the largest Illinois city that is not a county seat.

The city started in Kane County but now reaches into DuPage, Kendall and Will counties, which makes it one of only three Illinois cities that span four counties. That matters at closing, because the deed is recorded in the county where the parcel sits, and the property tax bill comes from that same county.

sections.h2: What are the West Side, East Side and Far East Side?
sections.html:
The Fox River divides the city physically, and the neighborhoods on each bank have their own history. Aurora began as two villages, East Aurora incorporated in 1845 and West Aurora organized in 1854, which joined as one city in 1857. Public buildings ended up around Stolp Island in the middle of the river because the two sides could not agree on a location.

  • The West Side lies west of the river.
  • The East Side runs east of the river up to the DuPage County line.
  • The Far East Side is the part of Aurora east of that line, in DuPage County.

The city is divided into ten wards, and the three regions also line up with police boundaries and school districts. When you describe a house to a buyer, name the side of the river, because it tells them the school district and the county in one phrase.

sections.h2: What kinds of older houses does Aurora have?
sections.html:
Aurora grew around the Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad, whose roundhouse and locomotive shop made it the largest employer until the 1960s. Waves of immigrants, including Luxembourgers who settled between 1850 and 1870, filled the neighborhoods near the factories.

The city has well-preserved Italianate and Queen Anne houses near downtown and Prairie School homes in the neighborhoods next to the core. It also has more than 50 Sears Catalog Homes and seven Lustron all-steel houses. An owner of one of those, or of any house built before the mid-twentieth century, should expect buyers to ask about knob-and-tube wiring, lead paint, old plumbing and foundation movement.

A cash offer for such a house is usually priced with the repairs in mind, while a listing buyer tends to raise them after the inspection.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Aurora houses?
sections.html:
Four public systems cover most of the city, and the district depends on the address.

  • West Aurora District 129 serves the west side of the river.
  • East Aurora District 131 serves the east side.
  • Indian Prairie District 204 serves the far eastern part in DuPage County.
  • Oswego District 308 has four schools inside Aurora's limits, and parts of the far north end of the city attend Batavia schools while a far southwest corner goes to Kaneland.

The Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy, a state-funded residential school for grades 10 to 12, also sits in the city. Aurora University and two Waubonsee Community College branches are also in the city.

sections.h2: Does Aurora's weather and flood history affect a house sale?
sections.html:
It can. Aurora has a humid continental climate with about 40 inches of precipitation a year. On July 17 and 18, 1996, a flood dropped 16.94 inches of rain in 24 hours, an Illinois record, and water reached almost every low-lying area and the neighborhoods bordering the Fox River.

Because of that history, buyers near the river tend to ask about basement water, sump pump age, and flood insurance. Gather any repair invoices and be open with buyers about past water. Ask the city's engineering staff or your insurer whether your parcel sits in a mapped flood zone.

sections.h2: What drives the Aurora economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Aurora has a long manufacturing tradition and sits on the edge of the Illinois Technology and Research Corridor. Past and present manufacturers include Caterpillar, Western Electric and Lyon Workspace Products, and the railroad shops once employed much of the East Side.

The Census Bureau's 2022 economic figures show $3.12 billion in retail sales and $1.42 billion in health care and social assistance receipts for the city, and the mean commute is 27.2 minutes. Downtown has the Paramount Theatre and the Hollywood Casino, and the city is home to Phillips Park Zoo and several museums.

  • Roughly 72% of residents aged 16 and over are in the labor force.
  • About 46% of residents age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home.
  • The city reports 26.4% of residents as foreign-born.

Those numbers describe a large, mixed city where buyers range from first-time families to investors, so a house in good condition on a quiet street draws different interest than a fixer on a busy corner.

sections.h2: What does Aurora's rental licensing mean if my house has tenants?
sections.html:
Every non-owner-occupied unit needs a license, and the city inspects each one every year, inside and out. The dwelling unit licensing program has existed since the city council adopted the Property Maintenance Code on June 1, 1982. Renewals are due each year by August 31, and the Property Standards Division sends renewal forms and schedules inspections by letter.

If you sell a licensed building, the code requires the new owner to be reported to the Operations Department within 3 working days. Property Standards is at 77 S Broadway, 1st Floor, and the number for the licensing program is 630-256-3770. The division also enforces codes on high weeds, junk and trash, unsafe stairs, illegal basement apartments and unregistered landlords, and it runs the city's vacant property licensing.

An inherited house that sits empty or a rental with a tenant who has left can draw a violation notice, so clear those before you list or accept an offer.

sections.h2: How are the deed and transfer tax handled on an Aurora sale?
sections.html:
Illinois collects its real estate transfer tax through revenue stamps that the county recorder sells, and the Department of Revenue says the stamp can also show payment of a county tax. Buyer and seller complete Form PTAX-203 and file it where the property is located.

A county may impose 25 cents per $500 of value, and home rule municipalities may add a tax of their own. Your title company can tell you which of these apply to a particular Aurora parcel and which side pays. Because the city lies in four counties, ask which county recorder handles your address before you schedule a signing.

faqs.q: Is Aurora in Kane County or DuPage County?
faqs.a: Both, and also parts of Kendall and Will counties. The city began in Kane County and later expanded, so the county for your house depends on its parcel number. That county records your deed and issues your tax bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a tenant-occupied house in Aurora?
faqs.a: The license belongs to the owner who rents the unit, and it is renewed each year by August 31. If you sell, the new ownership must be reported to the Operations Department within 3 working days. Call Property Standards at 630-256-3770 with questions about your account.

faqs.q: Will old flood damage hurt my sale?
faqs.a: It can, mostly because buyers worry about repeat water. Disclose past water problems in writing, keep repair records, and mention any sump pump or drainage work you completed. Near the Fox River, expect questions about flood insurance.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Aurora house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is, but you should know what is open before you sign. Contact Property Standards to learn what is open on your address and what it takes to close the case.

faqs.q: How do I choose between a listing and a cash offer?
faqs.a: Compare the net amount you would take home and the time each path needs. A listing can reach a higher price but adds repairs, showings and a buyer's financing risk, while a cash purchase trades price for a faster, more certain closing.
